bull.b: Exceptionally high and consistent free cash flow (FCF) provides durable financial flexibility. With FCF near $33B and ~97% cash conversion, Broadcom can fund R&D, secure supply, pay steady dividends, repurchase debt or shares, and support capital intensity of AI deployments without relying on external financing.

bull.t: Recurring Software Revenue & High Software Margins
bull.b: The software segment delivers high-margin, subscription-like economics with ARR growth (~17% YoY) and ~93% gross margins. This recurring revenue base smooths cyclical semiconductor swings, sustains consolidated margins and cash flow, and strengthens long-term revenue visibility through multi-year maintenance and licensing contracts.

bull.t: Strategic Customer Partnerships & Large AI Bookings
bull.b: Confirmed multi-year agreements and multi‑gigawatt commitments create durable demand visibility and competitive moats. Large bookings (> $30B) and hyperscaler design wins lock in multi-year supply, support scale advantages, and reduce customer churn risk, underpinning predictable revenue streams through 2028 and beyond.

bear.b: Rapid expansion is heavily concentrated in AI semiconductors, creating single-market dependency. If AI capex cycles, customer deployments or design choices slow, Broadcom’s top-line and margins could see outsized volatility. Limited non‑AI semiconductor growth reduces natural diversification over the medium term.

Although leverage ratios are manageable for a profitable firm, the large absolute debt stock (~$65B) constrains financial flexibility. High gross indebtedness raises refinancing, interest expense and covenant risks if macro or cash flow conditions deteriorate, and limits capacity for opportunistic M&A or cyclical cushion.

Elevated inventory and extended lead times reflect aggressive supply positioning for AI demand but increase working capital strain and execution risk. Large front‑loaded bookings and multi‑GW deployments require complex coordination; timing mismatches, supply hiccups or demand shifts could impair margins and cash conversion over several quarters.
